title: Roles Kernel
purpose: Provide the shared role execution kernel, typed semantic final-request evidence cutoff, and caller-owned structured result transport used by role flows.
summary: Current engineering runs belong to EngineeringRunService. roles.kernel supplies optional owner-built SLM binding via public/slm_binding.py and retains frozen legacy/explicit technical contracts; those legacy schemas are not admission requirements for new engineering runs.
invariants: New engineering execution is owned by roles.runtime.public.engineering_service.EngineeringRunService; old Factory/execute_role_session/RoleExecutionKernel writes cannot be a fallback.

The SLM producer keeps concrete model configuration and gateway ownership inside roles.kernel; KernelOne consumes only typed config/gateway protocols, and existing host bootstrap installs the binding lazily.
An explicit requested SLM configuration must govern the actual gateway. A warmed gateway with different model/base URL/provider/timeout cannot override it. Contract failures remain visible.
Cross-Cell callers use only roles.kernel public contracts; no external caller imports roles.kernel internal modules.

Caller-owned JSON result schemas enter through RoleStructuredOutputContractV1; the exact reserved result tool is audited and qualified as a non-executable provider protocol, while every executable or unknown tool remains subject to ToolSpecRegistry provenance; result payloads are locally validated and normalized before TransactionKernel can dispatch a tool or create an effect receipt.
FactoryRoleEvidenceCutoffAckV1 remains locator-only; resolve_cutoff_proof strictly reconstructs a detached FactoryRoleEvidenceCutoffProofV1 from committed authority facts.

B3.2 freezes the provider-visible semantic request after evidence injection; B3.3 propagates its exact runtime-private port through retry, fallback, and stream seams without authorizing physical provider transport.
Runtime-only cutoff authority ports never enter serializable provider requests, events, snapshots, or context packs.
B3.4-B3.5 must independently budget, conserve, snapshot, and qualify every role, retry, fallback, structured, stream, and Director fanout physical attempt before provider I/O.
All text file reads and writes use explicit UTF-8.

Prepared outcomes are durable recovery locators only; owner receipts, completion and continuation require a real committed outcome. Replay validates exact scope, stored payload and current head without repeating tools or provider calls.
